glossary_v1.plain_explanation_en: Postponed indefinitely, with no new date fixed yet.
The hearing has been postponed to a later date.
The court has started hearing the case but hasn't finished; it will continue later, usually with the same judge.
Scheduled for lawyers to present their case to the judge.
Placed in a general category for minor or procedural matters, not necessarily the main case hearing.
The case has been concluded by the court — this does not automatically mean you lost.
The case was thrown out because a required person did not show up in court.
A decision made with only one side present, because the other side did not appear.
A temporary order that applies until the court makes its final decision.
A court order that pauses or halts an action from happening.
The specific remedy or outcome a party is asking the court to grant.
The court has formally informed the other party and asked them to respond.
The court's attempt to officially notify someone failed — they could not be reached.
An official document ordering someone to appear in court.
Moved to a different judge or courtroom, usually for administrative reasons.
The court does not have the legal authority to hear this particular case.
A request asking the court to excuse a missed deadline.
A formal document authorizing a lawyer to represent someone in court.
The formal written response a party files to answer the claims made against them.
A written reply responding to the other party's written statement.
Sent back to a lower court for the case to be reconsidered.
A higher court has agreed to formally review the case again.
A request asking a higher court to review and correct an error in a lower court's decision.
The court has ruled that this case or appeal cannot legally proceed as filed.
Advance protection from arrest, requested before an arrest actually happens.
A court order keeping a person in custody for a specified period during investigation or trial.
A request to formally enforce a court's earlier decision (e.g., recovering money owed).
A document proving that an earlier court order has actually been followed.

notes.source: Derived from the 50-phrase eCourts/NJDG terminology test (Week 1, Tuesday)
